newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU oilseed producers seek new accord with U.S..
newsitem.headline: EU oilseed producers seek new accord with U.S..

text.p: European oilseeds producers will aim to renegotiate area limits under a transatlantic trade accord in the next world trade round, Philippe Dusser of French oilseeds producer federation FOP said on Thursday.
He told the Lipidex 97 oilseeds conference it was necessary to mobilise global area resources in order to meet expanding demand.
Limits on EU acreage therefore no longer made sense.
"I hope we will change that in the next WTO (World Trade Organisation) round," Dusser said.
European feeds industries supported this demand because the 30 million tonnes of protein meals that were imported represented 70 percent of the EU's total demand.
The rate was 63 percent 10 years ago and looked set to rise, which should increasingly expose EU producers to volatility in raw materials prices.
EU consumers were also looking to include more vegetable protein in their diet, which would raise demand for locally produced oils.
The Blair House Agreement, signed in December 1992 between the EU and the U.S., limits the EU oilseeds area to 4.934 million hectares based on a compulsory 10 percent set-aside.
But rising demand for vegetable oils and meals was also expected in overseas markets, which were potential buyers of EU seeds, oils and meals, Dusser said.
The U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation in projections up until 2010 placed 60 percent of the world's newly created economic wealth in Asia, he said.

Of the total, 25 percent of the newly acquired purchasing power should be located in China, which had already doubled its per capita meat use to 40 kg in recent years and was aiming for perhaps 50 kg by 2010.
China would need vast amounts of oilseed meal to achieve its meat output targets, and EU producers hoped to benefit from this.
